column8: Graph rerank text refresh can recover from the already materialized SearchResult via graphCandidateTextNode; it returns that usable bounded text after a point error, so this optional refresh is not a required hydration failure.

Public relationship search hydrates each candidate through the service's issued Engine.GetEdge. A genuine not-found may prune a stale/hidden hit; any other storage failure returns searchReadFailure rather than an empty or partially successful search response.

The relationship predicate's start endpoint is read on the same issued Engine. Hard read failure terminates public SearchRelationships, while true not-found preserves the predicate's existing missing-endpoint behavior. No physical adapter is used for hydration.

The relationship predicate's end endpoint independently propagates hard failures through searchReadFailure. The predicate runs only after those errors are handled; missing/hidden endpoints retain their existing visibility semantics.

VectorSearchCandidates returns candidate-filter storage errors from its adaptive search callback through the public error channel before constructing candidates. Filtering still uses the service's bound read owner; #1679 cancellation and diagnostics remain in the adaptive search owner.

The public vector candidate API passes an error-returning predicate callback to the existing adaptive owner and returns its error before constructing SearchCandidate values; it retains the existing index scoring policy.

Adaptive BM25 completion delegates its still-unfilled page to completeBM25Search and returns all three values; completion callback failures now use that same return instead of a second local error sink.

Adaptive vector widening delegates the remaining exact scan to completeVectorSearch with the same callback and statistics; its error already reaches the caller, and the callback now carries required storage failures explicitly.

Stage-two rerank hydration now calls the required point consumer and returns the failure through the existing rerankOutcome.failure. The hybrid caller makes that storage failure terminal while retaining ordinary reranker-backend fallback.

The ordinary batch fallback iterates requested IDs using the retained issued-view point adapter; it omits only ErrNotFound, returns other point failures, and never switches to a recovered bare provider.

Property filtering calls the required point owner for each indexed ID; missing nodes still skip, while an unrecovered storage error returns before opts.admitsNode can turn unreadable data into rejected rows.
Type filtering resolves each indexed ID through readSearchNode; it preserves label/property matching and missing-node skips, but returns a read failure before producing a successful filtered prefix.

Combined filtering batches only the unique type-admitted IDs through the common batch owner. An error enters the existing point-retry branch, whose typed error result is now checked; it does not impose a new blanket retry policy.

The combined filter retries unresolved type predicates via filterByType after a batch error and checks its returned error. Successfully recovered point reads keep the old retry outcome; failed point reads terminate filtering.

After a batch failure, the combined filter retries property predicates through filterByProperties and returns its error. This is the real public Search empty-success bypass covered by the release fault schedules.
Candidate type filtering now returns the required read error rather than continuing past an unreadable candidate. Nil for legitimate missing/hidden nodes retains the existing exclusion policy.

Full-text-only search passes candidate-filter failures through adaptiveBM25Search and returns before enrichment. Later hydration has its own propagated error; an unrecovered read cannot be accepted as a successful empty full-text result.
The BM25-only entry consumes the existing adaptive BM25 error return before materialization. The callback is now capable of carrying failed predicate reads to that checked return.
BM25 materialization checks enrichIndexResults error before assigning ranks or returning SearchResponse, so its existing public Search terminal observes required hydration failures.

The once closure installs one point function over the originally issued Engine and its common BoundReadOperation. Execution uses live admission plus that exact issued fallback; the installed adapter never substitutes an unwrapped provider.

sync.Once guards structural point-adapter binding for the immutable Service Engine. The public 4-versus40-row schedule measures fixed provider-source visits rather than discovery for every returned row.
Subsequent point reads invoke the retained bound function directly. Structural request-mask and dependency discovery happen in the once closure, while ExecuteBoundRead keeps the live guard.

The hybrid BM25 worker callback applies the existing decay rule then returns combined filter errors. Its bm25RetrievalResult carries that error back to the hybrid coordinator rather than a valid empty result.
The hybrid BM25 retrieval closure returns the adaptive owner error alongside rows/timing/statistics; the hybrid coordinator checks it before fusing results, preserving its worker/join ownership.
The hybrid vector callback preserves decay filtering and forwards combined predicate errors through the existing adaptive error return; no successful empty candidate substitution remains.

Hybrid vector retrieval consumes adaptiveVectorSearch pipelineErr, including its newly explicit predicate failures, before fusion. The outer Search terminal recognizes required-read errors and retains its backend-only fallback policy.
The hybrid coordinator checks enrichResults error before constructing the response or caching a page. The existing Search named-error terminal remains the diagnostic owner.

Vector-only search returns the error from the bound candidate filter/adaptive vector owner before selecting its method message or enrichment. The existing pipeline cancellation owner remains unchanged; retries may recover reads but cannot hide a terminal failure.
Vector-only materialization returns enrichIndexResults hydrateErr before setting ranks or assembling SearchResponse, so unreadable mandatory nodes cannot become an empty successful page.
Vector-only retrieval checks the existing adaptive error return before materialization; passing an error-returning predicate callback closes the former loss between filtering and this check.

Search construction stores the exact issued Engine and separately binds its read-operation methods once. It does not replace the stored data view with a discovered provider; subsequent hydration and callbacks use that issued view and its live policy.

Index materialization obtains aligned nodes from hitNodes and immediately returns its error before projection and search-match attachment. Result IDs and scores still retain their existing ordering/deduplication.
RRF materialization obtains aligned nodes through hitNodes and returns its error before projecting or enriching any public results. It preserves the existing visibility projection lease.
Required hit hydration calls the common batch helper when supported and makes an unrecovered batch error terminal. A missing map entry still invokes the orphan policy and keeps its aligned nil slot.

When a batch capability is unavailable, required hit hydration iterates readSearchNode, preserves aligned missing entries, and returns the first unrecovered point failure instead of an empty successful result.

The required point consumer calls the once-bound issued-view light reader, checks the existing searchBatch cancellation boundary, and delegates only ErrNotFound handling to the existing orphan policy; every other storage failure remains in the error chain.

Exact vector Where evaluation obtains its candidate node through readSearchNode and returns errors before evaluating the predicate; missing nodes still skip, while required failures no longer masquerade as a false Where result.

Indexed vector query postprocessing returns combined predicate errors directly after its existing supplement/scoring checks. One explicit adaptive error return replaces the former callback error side channel.
The indexed vector query consumes the adaptive owner error before building VectorQueryHit values. Supplement errors, scoring errors and predicate read errors now share that existing checked return.
